premises.text: Satellites have only one tank of fuel; when fuel runs out or orbits are wrong they must be destroyed, destroying large amounts of capital and revenue
premises.evidence_span: In the last decade, almost 200 satellites worth about 100 billion dollars have had to be destroyed because they've run out of fuel

premises.text: Drop-in replacement fueling port enables safe, reliable, self-aligning on-orbit refueling without expensive robotic attendants
premises.evidence_span: This fueling port allows satellites to be refueled safely and reliably in orbit

premises.text: OrbitFab launches tanks on available vehicles and manages orbital logistics to deliver the right fuel to customers when needed
premises.evidence_span: We build tanks, we put them onto any available launch vehicle so we get the best deal putting them into space. In space, we manage the logistics and the orbital mechanics, and we deliver the right fuel to our customers when they need them

value.text: Stop throwing satellites away by enabling on-orbit refueling that recovers lost satellite value
value.evidence_span: It is time to stop throwing satellites away

secondary_value.text: Customers can save ~50% CapEx; provider targets high gross margins
secondary_value.evidence_span: Our customers can save 50 percent on their capital expenditure, and we take home gross margins of 90 percent

causal_links.evidence_span: we have the opportunity to recover billions of dollars of lost revenue
Because this is a drop-in replacement, we're getting rapid customer adoption
we're building gas stations in space

notes: Catch-22 framing motivates fueling port as separately sold enabling module vs tanker logistics service (split). Alignment arms and ISS water demo folded into port/logistics mechanisms. Heinlein solar-system vision not coded as premise (rule 4).
